notes:
Account background: Auriga Medical AI builds diagnostic and clinical decision support assistants integrated into EHRs. Heavy regulatory constraints — must support data residency and strict audit trails. Evaluating Redwood Dedicated to move latency-sensitive inference off of cloud-managed endpoints and into reserved GPU pools (private VPC + occasional on-prem for DR).

Primary stakeholders: CTO (Priya Menon), Head of Infrastructure (Aaron Cho), Director of Clinical AI (Dr. Ellen Park). Priya: 'Need predictable latency and an SLA we can present to hospitals.' Aaron: focusing on region-level failover and cross-AZ headroom.

Technical requirements / ask (from evaluation calls):
- Workloads: secure chat assistant for clinicians (context windows 2k-8k tokens), near-real-time summarization of visit notes, embeddings for chart search.
- Latency SLOs: p95 < 250ms for short prompts (<512 tokens) for clinician chat, p95 < 600ms for larger summarization jobs; p99 targets discussed for alerts.
- Throughput: baseline 700 concurrent chat sessions (spiky peak ~1.5k), embedding throughput target 10k queries/min during daily indexing windows.
- Model preferences: running a mix of 13B-70B open models; exploring quantized variants for cost. Wants ability to pin model versions and fallback to trimmed variants.
- GPU sizing ask: estimate starting reserve = 24 x A100 80GB equivalent GPUs across three regions (8 GPUs per region) with 20% failover headroom and cross-region routing policies. Request detail on mapping: 8 reserved in us-east, 8 in us-west, 8 in eu-west with durable KV cache replication strategy.
- Failover/headroom: desire automatic failover if a region loses >40% capacity; need warm spare capacity reserved or cold-standby launch window < 5 minutes. Discussed options: hot hot reserved pools vs reserved + burst to hosted.
- Availability / SLA: target 99.95% regional availability for Dedicated pools; want explicit latency SLOs (p95/p99) tied to credits. Legal wants clear RTO for region failover and service degradation definitions.
- Observability: token-level billing, per-model latency breakdown, per-route error breakdown. Need audit logs forwarded to their SIEM and long-term retention for compliance.
